workday.apideck_credentials_note: Authentication is per consumer rather than per application, so there are no app-level credentials for Apideck to provide.
workday.consumer_access_level: Administrator with privileges to create Integration System Users and manage security groups and domain security policies
workday.difficulty_reason: Custom Auth + Manual Per-Consumer Setup + Complex Permissions
workday.authentication_note: A per-consumer Integration System User (ISU); not OAuth.
workday.rate_limits: No published hard limits; Workday throttles under high tenant load.
workday.sandbox_note: Testing runs against a consumer's own Workday tenant — no free trial, and Development tenants are contract-gated to existing Workday customers.
workday.webhooks: Virtual webhooks — no native webhooks in Workday; Apideck polls employees, applicants, jobs, bills, suppliers, purchase orders, and customers.

xero.sandbox_note: Free via Xero Developer Portal (demo company included).
important_to_know: Connection caps are tier-based: 5 active connections on the free Starter tier, 50 on Core, and more only from Plus upward. Certification unlocks the higher tiers but itself requires at least 10 active customer connections, so start the process before you hit the cap.
Refresh tokens expire after 60 days if unused — consumer must re-authorise.
Consumers can install a maximum of 2 uncertified apps — if at the limit they must remove another uncertified app first.
Certification compliance requires hiding the Apideck callback — a custom Vault domain must be configured before certification.

From March 2, 2026 the Journals API is gated to the Advanced tier and new apps must use granular OAuth scopes; older apps must migrate by September 2027. General-ledger reads need accounting.journals.read, which Apideck no longer requests by default; manual journals still work.
xero.rate_limits: 60 calls/minute and 5 concurrent calls per organisation; daily cap of 1,000 calls on Starter and 5,000 on Core and above; 10,000 calls/minute app-wide.
xero.partnership_note: App Partner Program certification is mandatory from the Plus tier and to list on the Xero App Store; Starter and Core tiers need no approval.
xero.webhooks: Native — invoice and bill events (created and updated).
xero.consumer_access_level: Standard or Adviser level user (Admin recommended for full data access)

environment_notes.description: Xero uses the same credential structure for sandbox and production — the connected Xero organisation determines which data is accessed. Testing options: the Xero Demo Company (included with every developer account, sample data) and a 30-day full-featured free trial via xero.com/signup.
When a consumer authorises your app, they choose which Xero organisation to connect. Consumers with multiple organisations require a separate connection per organisation.

responsibility_matrix.customer: ✓ (if scaling to the Plus tier or above)

xero.difficulty_reason: Self-Service OAuth + App Partner Certification Required to Scale
xero.costs: Free Starter tier; Core ~$22, Plus ~$152, Advanced ~$895 USD/month by connection count; Enterprise custom; plus per-GB egress overage. Effective March 2, 2026.

important_to_know: Turning on web service access is not something your consumer does alone — it is a domain feature their accountant or administrative office switches on. Build that hand-off into onboarding and confirm it is enabled before a consumer tries to connect.

Each operation opens a Yuki session before the request itself, so one Unify call becomes two calls to Yuki. Yuki does not document whether the session call counts against the daily quota, so size capacity conservatively.

On the free Minimal bundle the Sales web service has to be added as an accountant feature on top of general web service access; the paid bundles include it. Worth confirming with a Minimal-bundle consumer before you plan an invoicing flow.
yuki.webhooks: No webhooks — Yuki documents no event or subscription mechanism, and this connector adds no virtual webhooks, so poll for changes.
yuki.account_type_required: Yuki account on any bundle, including the free Minimal bundle, with web service access activated on the domain.

responsibility_matrix.area: Activate Web Service Access on the Yuki Domain
Generate Web Service Key & Set Its Access Rights

yuki.rate_limits: 1,000 web service calls per day per domain; paid add-ons raise the ceiling.
yuki.partnership_note: There is no app registration, review or partner agreement for Yuki's web services.
yuki.consumer_access_level: A user with the Portal administrator or Management role — only those roles can create web service keys.
yuki.authentication_note: A WebserviceAccessKey; not OAuth, and no redirect for your consumer to complete.
yuki.apideck_credentials_note: Each consumer connects with their own web service key, so there is no shared Apideck application.
yuki.sandbox_note: Yuki's free Minimal bundle is a real account, not a test environment; there is no developer sandbox or demo administration.

environment_notes.description: Testing and production share the same credentials — Yuki has no separate host for either. Test against a real Yuki administration you control, and pick the region (Netherlands or Belgium) that matches it. Treat everything you write as production data.

yuki.costs: Free to 1,000 calls/day. Above that: EUR 10.50/month for 1,001-5,000 calls/day, EUR 105/month for 5,001-10,000 — added by the consumer's accountant.

zoho-books.webhooks: Virtual webhooks — created/updated/deleted events on 10 resources, including invoices, bills, payments, customers and suppliers.
zoho-books.costs: Free — Zoho charges nothing for API access on any Zoho Books plan, including the Free plan.
zoho-books.rate_limits: 100 requests/minute per organization; daily cap set by the consumer's plan (1,000 Free to 10,000 Premium); 5 concurrent calls on Free, 10 on paid plans.
zoho-books.account_type_required: Active Zoho Books subscription (Free plan or higher)
zoho-books.sandbox_note: Start a free Zoho Books trial or add a dedicated test organization to your own account; there is no separate sandbox environment.
important_to_know: Zoho hosts each organization in one of seven regional data centres (US, EU, IN, AU, JP, CA, SA — verified June 2026). Apideck resolves the right region during authorization.
A Zoho Books account can hold several organizations and each is authorized separately, so a consumer running three organizations needs three connections.

Each consumer's own Zoho Books subscription sets their daily API quota, not yours — you cannot raise it for them. Design syncs around the lowest tier your consumers run on; heavier users unlock more frequent syncs by upgrading their own plan.
Refresh tokens never expire, but Zoho stores at most 20 per user: authorizing a 21st silently revokes the oldest, which can break a long-standing connection with no error or warning.
zoho-books.apideck_credentials_note: For testing: the OAuth consent screen shows "Apideck"; use your own Zoho OAuth client for production.

environment_notes.description: Zoho Books uses the same credentials for testing and production — there is no distinct-credential sandbox tier. To test, start a free Zoho Books trial at https://www.zoho.com/books/signup/ or add a dedicated test organization to your own Zoho Books account. A dedicated test organization is the safer choice during development, since anything else you connect is live production data.

zoho-books.partnership_note: No partner programme — self-service OAuth client registration is free. An optional Zoho Marketplace listing adds discoverability, not API access.
zoho-books.consumer_access_level: A user with organization-level access in the Zoho Books organization being authorized

zoho-crm.authentication_note: Authorization Code flow via Zoho Accounts.
zoho-crm.consumer_access_level: Any user whose profile has the Zoho CRM API Access permission (Administrators have it by default)
important_to_know: Zoho runs nine data centres (US, EU, India, Australia, Japan, China, Canada, Saudi Arabia, UK). Your client needs Multi-DC enabled for every data centre your consumers' accounts live in, or their authorisation fails; the connector detects each consumer's data centre itself.

Zoho keeps at most 20 refresh tokens per user per client and 15 live access tokens per refresh token: a 21st authorisation by the same user silently invalidates the oldest connection. Refresh tokens otherwise never expire unless revoked.
Your consumers' other Zoho apps draw on the same daily credit pool as your integration, so a busy organisation can throttle your sync well before its edition's headline limit.
Zoho's Sandbox feature is included only from the Enterprise edition up, so a consumer on a lower edition has no test copy of their org.
zoho-crm.partnership_note: No partner programme and no app review: you register a Server-based client yourself.
zoho-crm.account_type_required: Any Zoho CRM edition, including Free
zoho-crm.difficulty_reason: Self-Service OAuth Client + Free Edition for Testing, No Review or Partnership
zoho-crm.costs: None. Registering a Zoho API client is free and API calls draw on the consumer's own edition credits.
zoho-crm.webhooks: No webhooks — Zoho CRM changes are not surfaced as Apideck events; sync by polling the CRM and Lead APIs

responsibility_matrix.area: Register a Server-based client in the Zoho API console
Enable Multi-DC for the data centres your consumers use
Add Client ID, Client Secret and scopes in the Apideck Dashboard
Token refresh, credential storage and data-centre routing
Maintain the connector and unified CRM and Lead APIs

environment_notes.description: One Zoho API client serves testing and production. Zoho separates environments at the organisation level: a production org, a Sandbox org (on its own sandbox API domain) and a Developer Edition org are each authorised separately, and a token issued for one organisation cannot call another. Apideck's temporary shared test credentials are an alternative for early evaluation (request access via https://help.apideck.com/en/articles/7774658). Take care when testing against a production org.

zoho-crm.rate_limits: Daily credits per org by edition: 5,000 (Free) to 50,000 plus 250 to 2,000 per user (paid); 5 to 25 concurrent calls; HTTP 429 on excess
zoho-crm.sandbox_note: A Free edition org for your own testing, or a Developer Edition org by invitation from a sandbox-enabled customer.
zoho-crm.apideck_credentials_note: The Zoho consent screen shows "Apideck"; use your own Zoho client in production.
